govdocs-archive_org-narcissus-and-goldmu: Hermann Hesse’s Narcissus and Goldmund — 1930 — contrasts the monk and the wanderer: spirit against senses. The novel is Hesse’s great fable of the divided self. Goldmund’s wanderings are unforgettable. The medieval setting glows. The book remains a beloved classic.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBIControl_FBI_: Andy Purdy’s memorandum on the search for missing autopsy materials is a congressional file. The missing materials fueled suspicion. Purdy served the committee. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBIDomesticInte: Joseph McLellan’s Bertolt Brecht by J. Edgar Hoover covers the FBI’s file on the playwright. The Bureau watched artists for years. Brecht fled the inquisitors. The file is a curiosity. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GaleWilliamCol_: This G-man chat with George Saudikas Jr. — November 9, 1963 — is a Bureau file. The opened chat is a first-hand source. The Bureau cast a wide net before Dallas. Bookmen prize such files. The file fits the government shelf.
entertainments-for-home-church-and-schoo: Frederica Seeger put together this handy book of recitations, dialogues, tableaux, and short plays for home talent. Made for parlors, Sunday schools, and classrooms, it gave plain folk ready-made programs for holidays and glad days. A sweet look at how families made their own fun long ago.
the-purple-parasol: George Barr McCutcheon weaves a romantic tale around a mysterious purple parasol and the charming young woman who carries it. Mistaken identities, society balls, and a hero smitten at first sight carry the story at a merry pace. Pure McCutcheon — light, gallant, and designed to make readers smile.
the-bride-of-fort-edward-founded-on-an-i: Delia Salter Bacon — of Shakespeare-authorship fame — writes this Revolutionary romance of the bride of Fort Edward. Love and war mingle in her earnest, old-fashioned tale. A curiosity from a remarkable woman. Jane McCrea's tragic fate inspired this earnest tale of wartime love.
short-stories-and-selections-for-use-in-: Emilie Kip Baker selects short stories and passages for high-school readers — the best of many authors, chosen to teach and delight. A thoughtful anthology for the classroom. Good reading, well chosen. Hawthorne, Poe, and many more instruct and entertain in turn.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-dioce: This 1913 reference article on the ancient diocese of Bristol — Henry VIII's new see. Edwin Burton gives its story. The abbey became a cathedral. Its bishops served the west country. A Tudor foundation, still standing. Its chapter keeps the old customs.
